name: Integers
summary: The ring of integers modulo m (m at least 2); R!x maps an integer, or a rational with a unit denominator, into it.

examples.code: R := Integers(12); x := R!5; x * 7; x^-1; Order(x); IsUnit(R!4);

differs: Integers(1), the zero ring, is refused.
Order of a residue modulo an m of more than 128 bits is refused.
A collection of residues coerces assignments only when its universe is declared: [R | 1, 7] takes Q[2] := 13, but [R!1, 7] refuses it.
Append and Include of an integer to a collection of residues are refused, even with a declared universe [R | ...] or {R | ...}.

name: Sym
summary: The symmetric group on 1 .. n; G!(1, 2, 3) or G![2, 3, 1] makes a permutation p, and i^p is the image of i.
differs: Iterating over Sym(n) gives its permutations in Sagebrush's own (lexicographic) order, not Magma's.

PermutationGroup< n | ... >, sub< G | ... >, Alt(n) and CyclicGroup(n) are permutation groups too; their intersections (meet), Generators(G), printing PermutationGroup< ... > itself (its second value, a map) and printing a permutation group whose generators are longer than a line are not supported yet.

name: DihedralGroup
summary: The dihedral group of order 2n (n >= 3) as permutations of 1 .. n: G.1 the rotation (1, 2, ..., n), G.2 the reflection i -> n + 1 - i.

examples.code: G := DihedralGroup(4); #G; G.1*G.2; G.2^2; Order(G.1); G!(1, 3)(2, 4);

differs: Iterating over a dihedral group, and its subgroups and other structure (Center, Generators), are not supported yet.
A generator longer than a line is not printed (Magma wraps it).
DihedralGroup(3) is Sym(3), as in Magma; its reflection is (1, 2). G.-1 (an inverse by its index) is not supported yet.

name: Alt
summary: The alternating group on 1 .. n, with Magma's generators.

name: CyclicGroup
summary: The cyclic group of order n as permutations of 1 .. n, generated by (1, 2, ..., n).

name: Orbits
summary: The orbits of a permutation group on its points, smallest first, each from its least point.

name: Orbit
summary: The orbit of a point, in the order its points are reached.

name: Stabilizer
summary: The subgroup of a permutation group fixing a point.
differs: A computed subgroup's generators are Sagebrush's own (the same group as Magma's, other generators), and so is the order of the points within its orbits.

name: IsTransitive
summary: Whether a permutation group is transitive on its points.

name: IsAbelian
summary: Whether a permutation group is abelian.

name: IsSolvable
summary: Whether a permutation group is solvable.

name: DerivedSubgroup
summary: The commutator subgroup of a permutation group.
differs: A computed subgroup's generators are Sagebrush's own (the same group as Magma's, other generators), and so is the order of the points within its orbits.

name: Ngens
summary: The number of generators of a permutation group.

name: ConjugacyClasses
summary: Sym(n)'s conjugacy classes as tuples <order, length, representative>, in Magma's order, printed as Magma's table.

examples.code: G := Sym(4); #ConjugacyClasses(G); ConjugacyClasses(G)[3]; [c[2] : c in ConjugacyClasses(G)];

differs: The order and representatives are checked against Magma for n up to 30; a larger n runs the same rule, as far as memory allows.
Only the symmetric groups (and DihedralGroup(3), which is Sym(3)): another dihedral group's classes are refused, since Magma's representatives there come from its own algorithm.
The table inside another value ([C], <C>) or in a string (Sprint) is refused: Magma lays it out in ways of its own.

name: IsIsomorphic
summary: Whether two quadratic fields, or the symmetric and dihedral groups, are isomorphic; fields of two degrees are not.

examples.code: b := IsIsomorphic(QuadraticField(-1), QuadraticField(-4)); b; IsIsomorphic(Sym(4), DihedralGroup(12)); IsIsomorphic(QuadraticField(2), QuadraticField(3));

differs: Only number fields of degree 2 (or of two degrees), and Sym(n) and DihedralGroup(n); other structures and number fields of a higher degree are refused.
The second value, the isomorphism, is not given: printing a true result and b, f := ... with true are refused (with false Magma gives none either).

name: Identity
summary: The identity element of a symmetric group.

name: Graph
summary: A graph on the vertices 1 .. n with the given edges (a constructor).
alternative: Sage mode's Graph, e.g. G = Graph({1: [2, 3], 2: [3]}), with is_connected(), connected_components(), shortest_path(), is_tree() and spanning_trees_count()
